newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 1.

text.p: Japan Satellite Broadcasting Inc, Japan's top private satellite broadcaster, plans to cut its capital by about 90 percent from 41.56 billion yen to 4.15 billion yen at the end of March, 1997. It plans to use the funds to reduce its accumulated loss, which reached 78.1 billion yen at the end of March, 1996. It plans to clear accumulated losses entirely within the business year starting April 1999, and pay dividends that year. It also hopes to list its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange by 2000.

Japanese auto and electrical equipment manufacturers plan to expand their task-sharing among subsidiaries in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members to benefit from a preferential tariff plan to be introduced by the ASEAN on Friday. The manufacturers will be able to cut a large amount of their production costs under the plan. Nippondenso Co Ltd is setting up a production role-sharing system among its subsidiaries in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines. Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd plans to reorganise its Asian production.

Nikon Corp plans to increase its sales of 64-megabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) in the business year starting April 1997 by about four times from this year. Advantest Corp also plans to expand sales of testing equipment used in the high-speed memory chips.
